derivation: Combines the requirement to start from real weekly context with the prior-work example's full context snapshot.
statement: Begin by extracting the user's weekly objective, available training days, equipment, recent training pattern, and recovery notes before selecting any session structure.

derivation: Turns the primary-adaptation rule and the case example's preserved pulling priority into an ordering rule for the week.
statement: Choose one primary adaptation for the week, place its highest-priority exposure when fatigue is lowest, and keep supporting work only when it serves that adaptation or a clear constraint.

derivation: Combines executable-session requirements with substitution-by-function requirements.
statement: For every training day, specify exercise, sets, reps or duration, effort target, rest guidance, and an allowed substitution that still matches the intended function and achievable effort.

derivation: Combines recovery-trend logic with the prior-work example's choice to remove optional lower-body volume first.
statement: When sleep, soreness, and performance trend downward across sessions, reduce the next session's optional volume before changing the whole block, while keeping the main movement pattern if it remains tolerable.

derivation: Unifies the explicit pain boundary, the prior-work revision, and the product boundary statement.
statement: If pain appears, stop or substitute aggravating movements, shift to pain-free work when available, note uncertainty, and direct the user to a qualified clinician without diagnosing, rehabilitating, or claiming medical safety.

derivation: Combines missed-session recovery protection with the rule against filling all seven days for appearances.
statement: When schedule disruption removes a session, preserve the highest-priority exposure, move or drop lower-priority work, and protect recovery instead of compressing the week for completeness.

derivation: Combines substitution constraints with the primary-adaptation rule and tradeoff disclosure requirement.
statement: Use substitutions only when they can still deliver the intended stimulus; otherwise change set structure or exercise selection and explicitly explain the tradeoff created by equipment limits.

derivation: Combines observable-log evidence with the prior-work context example's concrete training data.
statement: If a training log lacks an effort rating, infer only from completed reps, load, missed reps, tempo breakdown, and the user's note, and state the uncertainty rather than inventing an RPE.
